questions.q: Fill up: Dizygotic twins form when ______, whereas monozygotic twins form when ______.
opts: 2 ova are fertilized by 2 different sperms; a single ovum fertilized by a single sperm divides into 2
1 ovum is fertilized by 2 sperms; 2 ova fuse
questions.exp: Dizygotic = 2 ova + 2 sperms → 2 zygotes; monozygotic = 1 ovum + 1 sperm → 1 zygote that divides. (Book p460)

questions.q: Which twin type is more common and what are they also called?
questions.exp: Dizygotic twins are more common and are called fraternal; monozygotic are identical. (Book p460)

questions.q: Which characteristics are SHARED by monozygotic twins but may differ in dizygotic twins?
opts: Sex, blood group, HLA typing and phenotyping – yet fingerprints differ
questions.exp: Monozygotic twins share sex, blood group, HLA and phenotype but have different fingerprints; dizygotic sex may differ. (Book p460)

questions.q: Match incidence of dizygotic twinning by country.
opts: Nigeria 1 in 20 (maximum), Japan 1 in 200 (least), India 1 in 80
Nigeria 1 in 200, Japan 1 in 20, India 1 in 800
questions.exp: Incidence: Nigeria 1:20 max, Japan 1:200 least, India 1:80. (Book p460)

questions.q: Monozygotic twinning incidence across the world is:
questions.exp: Monozygotic twinning is uniform worldwide (1 in 250). (Book p460)

questions.q: Hellin's rule states twins occur 1 in 80; triplets and quadruplets follow which pattern?
questions.exp: Hellin's rule: triplets 1 in 80² and quadruplets 1 in 80³. (Book p460)

questions.q: Two ova released in the SAME cycle but fertilized at different times by different acts of coitus is:
opts: Superfecundation – rare but seen in humans
questions.exp: Superfecundation = same-cycle ova fertilized at different times; it is rare but possible in humans. (Book p461)

questions.q: Superfetation (ova released and fertilized in DIFFERENT cycles) is:
opts: Not seen in humans – theoretically possible until the uterine cavity is obliterated at 14–16 weeks
questions.exp: Superfetation is not seen in humans; theoretically possible until cavity obliteration at 14–16 weeks. (Book p461)

questions.q: Risk factors for DIZYGOTIC twins include all EXCEPT:
opts: IVF only – geographical distribution, ↑ maternal age, ↑ parity and maternal family history are not risks
Maternal family h/o twins and ovulation-induction drugs (clomiphene, hMG)
questions.exp: Dizygotic risks: geography, ↑ age, ↑ parity, maternal family history, IVF and ovulation induction; IVF alone is the monozygotic risk. (Book p461)

questions.q: The only listed risk factor for MONOZYGOTIC twins is:
questions.exp: Monozygotic twinning risk lists IVF only. (Book p461)

questions.q: Zygosity refers to ______ while chorionicity refers to ______.
opts: Type of conception; type of placentation
Type of placentation; type of conception
Number of sacs; number of embryos
questions.exp: Zygosity = type of conception; chorionicity = type of placentation. (Book p461)

questions.q: Match the fetal membranes: chorion and amnion.
opts: Chorion – outer membrane formed on day 8; amnion – inner membrane formed on day 10
Chorion – inner, day 10; amnion – outer, day 8
questions.exp: Chorion is the outer membrane (day 8) and amnion the inner (day 10). (Book p461)

questions.q: Dizygotic twins always have which membrane arrangement?
opts: Dichorionic diamniotic – each twin with separate amnion and chorion
questions.exp: Dizygotic twins are DCDA with separate amnion and chorion each. (Book p461)

questions.q: Match division timing of a monozygotic zygote to its membrane pattern: <4 days (morula), 4–8 days (blastocyst), 8–12 days, ≥12 days.
questions.exp: <4 days DCDA; 4–8 days MCDA (common chorion by day 8); 8–12 days MCMA; ≥12 days conjoined twins. (Book p462)

questions.q: Division at 4–8 days (blastocyst stage) yields MCDA because:
opts: By day 8 a common chorion is already formed while amnions remain separate
The amnion forms before the chorion
questions.exp: Division after day 4 but before the common chorion/amnion sequence gives a shared chorion with two amnions. (Book p462)

questions.q: Division occurring after formation of the single amnion, chorion and embryonic disc (≥12 days) results in:
questions.exp: Late division after the embryonic disc forms produces conjoined/Siamese twins. (Book p462)

questions.q: Complications and management of monochorionic monoamniotic twins (which include all conjoined twins):
opts: Cord entanglement and sudden IUD of both twins; corticosteroids for lung maturity and C-section at 32–34 weeks
Nothing specific; vaginal delivery at term
questions.exp: MCMA carries cord entanglement and sudden double IUD; give steroids and deliver by C-section at 32–34 weeks. (Book p462)

questions.q: The m/c variety of twins overall and among monozygotic twins respectively are:
questions.exp: Overall m/c is DCDA; among monozygotic twins m/c is MCDA. (Book p462)

questions.q: Prognosis in twins depends primarily on:
questions.exp: Prognosis depends on chorionicity: monochorionic worse, dichorionic better. (Book p462)

questions.q: Determination of chorionicity: IOC and timing are:
questions.exp: Chorionicity is best determined by TVS at 10–14 weeks. (Book p462)

questions.q: Number of membrane layers between the twins in DCDA, MCDA and MCMA respectively:
questions.exp: DCDA 4 layers, MCDA 2 layers, MCMA none. (Book p463)

questions.q: Membrane thickness distinguishing DCDA from MCDA is:
opts: ≥ 2 mm in DCDA vs < 2 mm in MCDA
questions.exp: DCDA membranes are ≥2 mm thick while MCDA are <2 mm. (Book p463)

questions.q: Vascular connections between twins in DCDA, MCDA and MCMA are:
opts: Absent; deep vascular connections; superficial vascular connections
questions.exp: DCDA lacks connections; MCDA has deep connections (TTTS risk); MCMA has superficial ones. (Book p463)

questions.q: Placental number and USG sign in DCDA twins:
opts: 2 placentae (or appearing single) with twin peak/Lambda sign (placenta between chorions)
questions.exp: DCDA shows 2 placentae and the twin peak/Lambda sign with placenta between the chorions. (Book p463)

questions.q: The T sign on USG (single chorion with no intervening placenta) indicates:
questions.exp: T sign = single chorion without intervening placenta = MCDA. (Book p463)

questions.q: Specific complications of MCDA and MCMA respectively:
opts: TTTS (due to deep vascular connections); cord entanglement
questions.exp: MCDA → TTTS via deep connections; MCMA → cord entanglement. (Book p463)

questions.q: Delivery timing for DCDA, MCDA and MCMA twins:
opts: 38 weeks; 36 weeks; 32–34 weeks by C-section after corticosteroids
questions.exp: DCDA 38 weeks, MCDA 36 weeks, MCMA 32–34 weeks by C-section after steroids. (Book p463)

questions.sec: USG in twin pregnancy & conjoined twins
questions.q: USG in twin pregnancy is significant for assessing gestational age, chorionicity and ↑NT. Chorionicity can be determined earliest at ______ and best at ______.
questions.exp: Chorionicity: earliest 7 weeks, best 10 weeks. (Book p464)

questions.sec: USG in twin pregnancy & conjoined twins
questions.q: An increased nuchal translucency in a twin pregnancy raises suspicion of ______, and its ideal assessment time is the ______ trimester.
questions.exp: ↑NT suggests TTTS; the ideal time is the 2nd trimester. (Book p464)

questions.sec: USG in twin pregnancy & conjoined twins
questions.q: Which is NOT a marker of dichorionicity on USG?
questions.exp: Dichorionicity markers: ≥4 membranes, ≥2 mm thickness, different sexes, 2 placentae and twin peak sign. (Book p464)

questions.sec: USG in twin pregnancy & conjoined twins
questions.q: Conjoined twins are a complication of which twin type, and how are the types named?
opts: Monoamniotic twins; parapagus (lower abdomen/pelvis), thoracophagus (thorax), rachiphagus (vertebral column), craniophagus
questions.exp: Conjoined twins complicate monoamniotic pregnancies with the listed joining types. (Book p464)

questions.sec: USG in twin pregnancy & conjoined twins
questions.q: Management of conjoined twins is:
opts: C-section between 32–34 weeks after completing the steroid course
questions.exp: Deliver by C-section at 32–34 weeks after the steroid course. (Book p464)

questions.q: Maternal complications of twin pregnancy include pronounced haemodynamic changes, ↑ placental size, polyhydramnios and which liver conditions?
opts: Intrahepatic cholestasis and acute fatty liver of pregnancy
questions.exp: Intrahepatic cholestasis and acute fatty liver of pregnancy are listed maternal complications. (Book p465)

questions.q: Twin pregnancy increases the risk of which obstetric complications?
opts: Preterm labour, PROM, PPH, cord prolapse, malpresentations, pre-eclampsia, abruptio and placenta previa
questions.exp: All listed risks rise, including pre-eclampsia from ↑ paternal antigen exposure. (Book p465)

questions.q: ↑ hCG and ↑ human placental lactogen in twins explain which associations?
questions.exp: ↑hCG → hyperemesis; ↑hPL → gestational diabetes. (Book p465)

questions.q: Pre-eclampsia in twin pregnancy is attributed to:
questions.exp: The notes attribute pre-eclampsia to increased paternal antigen exposure. (Book p465)

questions.q: PIH prophylaxis in twin pregnancy uses:
opts: Low-dose aspirin 80–150 mg/day started before 16 weeks (ideal 12 weeks)
questions.exp: Low-dose aspirin 80–150 mg/day before 16 weeks (ideally 12) is the prophylaxis. (Book p465)

questions.q: Fetal complications are m/c in which order?
opts: Monochorionic > dichorionic and monozygotic > dizygotic (except cumulative chromosomal anomaly risk)
questions.exp: Complications are m/c in monochorionic and monozygotic twins, except cumulative chromosomal anomaly risk. (Book p465)

questions.q: For aneuploidy testing, sampling differs by zygosity how?
opts: Monozygotic – sample any one twin; dizygotic – sample both twins
Monozygotic – sample both; dizygotic – sample one
questions.exp: Monozygotic twins share genetics so one sample suffices; dizygotic need both sampled. (Book p465)

questions.q: Prognosis depends on chorionicity and amnionicity EXCEPT for which two complications?
opts: Preterm labour (related to number of twins) and IUGR
questions.exp: Preterm labour relates to twin number and IUGR is independent of chorionicity. (Book p465)

questions.q: Fetal reduction in multifetal pregnancy: DOC, target and timing are:
opts: Intracardiac KCl injection into the fetus with least chance of survival, at 10–13 weeks
Intracardiac KCl into the largest fetus at 20 weeks
Aspiration of amniotic fluid at 8 weeks
questions.exp: Intracardiac KCl to the least-viable fetus at 10–13 weeks; it does not affect the other fetus's survival. (Book p465)

questions.q: The three complications common to ALL twin pregnancies are:
opts: Preterm labour (m/c), IUGR and congenital anomalies
Cord prolapse, vasa previa and rupture
questions.exp: Preterm labour (m/c), IUGR and congenital anomalies affect all twins. (Book p466)

questions.q: In a primigravida twin pregnancy without history of preterm labour or 2nd-trimester abortion, cervical cerclage is:
questions.exp: The notes state cerclage is not done in this scenario. (Book p466)

questions.q: Congenital anomalies in twins are m/c compared with singletons and follow which pattern?
opts: Twin > singleton; monochorionic > dichorionic; heart defects
questions.exp: Anomalies are more common in twins, especially monochorionic, with heart defects highlighted. (Book p466)

questions.q: For TTTS screening in monochorionic twins, echocardiography is done at ______ and a target/anomaly/level II scan is done in ______.
questions.exp: Echo at 18–22 weeks; the level II scan applies to all pregnant women. (Book p466)

questions.q: Vanishing twin syndrome refers to ______ and is common in ______.
opts: Early spontaneous reduction of a twin pregnancy to singleton; IVF pregnancies
Death of both twins at term; spontaneous conception
Late IUD of one twin; natural conception
questions.exp: Vanishing twin = early spontaneous reduction to singleton, common after IVF. (Book p466)

questions.q: Effect of a vanishing twin on the surviving co-twin:
questions.exp: The second twin usually survives normally, ± LBW/SGA. (Book p466)

questions.q: After death of one twin, complications in the survivor depend on chorionicity how?
opts: Surviving monochorionic twin – complications (+) due to vascular anastomosis; surviving dichorionic twin – complications (−)
questions.exp: Vascular anastomoses transmit injury only in monochorionic survivors. (Book p466)

questions.q: In a dying monochorionic co-twin, the sequence in twin A (high-pressure system) flowing to twin B (low-pressure system) causes:
opts: Hypotension, anemia and exsanguination leading to death of twin A
questions.exp: Blood flows from the high-pressure twin A to twin B causing hypotension, anemia, exsanguination and death of twin A. (Book p466)

questions.q: Management when USG shows impending death of the 1st twin:
questions.exp: Impending death of the 1st twin mandates immediate delivery of both. (Book p467)

questions.q: The four complications specific to monochorionic twins are:
opts: TTTS, TAPS, TRAP and selective IUGR
Cord entanglement, conjoining, vanishing twin, show
questions.exp: TTTS, TAPS, TRAP and selective IUGR are monochorionic-specific. (Book p467)

questions.q: Differentiate IUGR from selective IUGR in twins.
opts: IUGR relates to twin number with both twins IUGR; selective IUGR is a monochorionic complication with one normal and one IUGR twin
Selective IUGR affects dichorionic twins only
questions.exp: General IUGR affects both twins (number-related); selective IUGR affects one monochorionic twin. (Book p467)

questions.q: TTTS occurs due to:
opts: Deep vascular anastomosis between artery and vein
questions.exp: Deep arterio-venous anastomoses cause TTTS. (Book p467)

questions.q: Prevalence of TTTS by chorionicity/amnionicity:
opts: MCDA m/c (deep anastomoses); MCMA l/c (superficial); DCDA not seen (no connections)
questions.exp: MCDA is m/c, MCMA less common and DCDA exempt. (Book p467)

questions.q: In TTTS, the DONOR twin shows which renal and fluid findings?
opts: ↓ renal blood flow (↑ renal failure risk), ↓ GFR and oligohydramnios
questions.exp: The donor has reduced renal perfusion and GFR with oligohydramnios; the recipient the opposite. (Book p467)

questions.q: Haemoglobin consequences in TTTS are:
opts: Donor – anemia with heart failure; recipient – polycythemia with thrombosis and congestive heart failure
questions.exp: Donor anemia/heart failure vs recipient polycythemia/thrombosis/CHF. (Book p467)

questions.q: Peak systolic velocity of the MCA in TTTS donor vs recipient:
questions.exp: MCA-PSV ≥1.5 MoM in the anemic donor and <0.8 MoM in the polycythemic recipient. (Book p467)

questions.q: Serious complications listed for TTTS fetuses are:
questions.exp: Hydrops fetalis and death are the listed complications. (Book p467)

questions.q: The best method for amniotic fluid assessment in twin pregnancy is:
opts: Single largest vertical pocket on USG
Amniotic fluid index summing four quadrants
questions.exp: The single largest vertical pocket is the best method in twins. (Book p468)

questions.q: Diagnostic criteria of TTTS in monochorionic diamniotic twins:
opts: Polyhydramnios in one twin with oligohydramnios in the other
questions.exp: Poly-oligo sequence between MCDA twins defines TTTS. (Book p468)

questions.q: The early marker of TTTS is:
questions.exp: Increased NT is the early marker of TTTS. (Book p468)

questions.q: The 'stuck twin' appearance in TTTS results from:
opts: RAAS activation in the donor twin to maintain intravascular volume/BP → oliguria, anuria, anhydramnios
questions.exp: Donor RAAS activation causes oliguria/anuria/anhydramnios, fixing the stuck twin. (Book p468)

questions.q: Quintero stage 1 vs stage 2 of TTTS differ by:
opts: Bladder visible (oliguria) in stage 1 vs not visible (anuria) in stage 2, both with normal Doppler
questions.exp: Stage 1: oligohydramnios with visible bladder; stage 2: bladder not visible; Doppler still normal in both. (Book p468)

questions.q: Match Quintero stages 3, 4 and 5.
opts: Stage 3 abnormal Doppler; stage 4 hydrops fetalis in one/both; stage 5 death of one/both twins
Stage 3 hydrops; stage 4 abnormal Doppler; stage 5 anuria
Stage 3 anuria; stage 4 Doppler; stage 5 hydrops
Stage 3 death; stage 4 hydrops; stage 5 Doppler
questions.exp: Stages 3–5 add abnormal Doppler, hydrops and death respectively. (Book p468)

questions.q: Follow-up Doppler studies in monochorionic twins are done at 16–20 weeks and include:
opts: Umbilical artery, vein, ductus venosus and PSV of MCA
questions.exp: Doppler at 16–20 weeks covers umbilical artery/vein, ductus venosus and MCA-PSV. (Book p469)

questions.q: USG follow-up in TTTS-risk twins assesses:
opts: Fetal biometry for growth, oligo/polyhydramnios and diagnosis of hydrops fetalis
questions.exp: USG tracks growth biometry, fluid discordance and hydrops. (Book p469)

questions.q: Echocardiography of the RECIPIENT twin in TTTS looks for:
opts: Pulmonary atresia/stenosis, hypertrophy and right-side > left-side dysfunction
questions.exp: Recipient echo shows pulmonary atresia/stenosis, hypertrophy and right > left dysfunction. (Book p469)

questions.q: Treatment of TTTS by gestational age: ≤28 weeks vs >28 weeks.
opts: Fetoscopic laser ablation of vascular anastomoses; serial amnioreduction
questions.exp: ≤28 weeks fetoscopic laser ablation; >28 weeks serial amnioreduction. (Book p469)

questions.q: TAPS is best described as:
opts: An atypical, milder, chronic form of TTTS due to slow RBC transfusion through few small (<1 mm) arterio-venous anastomoses
An acute severe form of TTTS
questions.exp: TAPS arises from slow transfusion across tiny (<1 mm) anastomoses, spontaneously or post-laser. (Book p469)

questions.q: TAPS can occur spontaneously or after which procedure?
questions.exp: TAPS may follow laser ablation of TTTS. (Book p469)

questions.q: Features of TAPS: haemoglobin, amniotic fluid and MCA-PSV.
opts: Donor anemia, recipient polycythemia; amniotic fluid NORMAL in both; PSV >1.5 MoM donor and <0.8 MoM recipient
questions.exp: Unlike TTTS, TAPS has normal amniotic fluid with anemia/polycythemia and discordant MCA-PSV. (Book p469)

questions.q: TRAP sequence is a rare complication of monochorionic twins caused by:
opts: An aberrant arterio-arterial anastomosis with twin A pumping deoxygenated blood via the umbilical artery to the acardiac twin B
questions.exp: Twin A's normal heart perfuses the acardiac twin B with deoxygenated blood through an aberrant arterio-arterial anastomosis. (Book p469)

questions.q: Outcomes in the acardiac twin of TRAP are named:
opts: Acardiac acephalus (only lower part developed) and acardiac amorphous (amorphous mass, no parts)
questions.exp: Acardiac acephalus has only the lower part developed; acardiac amorphus is an amorphous mass. (Book p470)

questions.q: Selective IUGR is defined by fetal weight < 10th percentile of the normal co-twin OR:
questions.exp: Discordance >25% in weight also defines selective IUGR. (Book p470)

questions.q: Causes of selective IUGR listed are:
opts: Unequal placental sharing and unequal splitting of the initial cell mass
questions.exp: Unequal placental sharing or unequal splitting of the initial cell mass causes selective IUGR. (Book p470)

questions.q: Complications specific to MONOAMNIOTIC twins and the cause of cord entanglement:
opts: Cord entanglement and conjoined twins; true knots form the cause
questions.exp: Monoamniotic twins face cord entanglement (true knots) and conjoining. (Book p470)

questions.q: Management of monoamniotic twins with cord entanglement risk:
questions.exp: C-section at 32–34 weeks is advised. (Book p470)

questions.q: The 1st twin is defined as the one that:
opts: Is closer to the internal os during pregnancy / comes out first during delivery
Is labelled by the sonologist arbitrarily
questions.exp: The twin closer to the internal os (delivered first) is the 1st twin. (Book p471)

questions.q: The m/c and 2nd m/c presentation combinations in twins are:
questions.exp: Both-vertex is m/c; 1st vertex + 2nd breech is second m/c. (Book p471)

questions.q: Interlocking of twins is seen with which combination and is managed by:
questions.exp: Interlocking occurs when the 1st is breech and 2nd cephalic; C-section is done. (Book p471)

questions.q: Mode of delivery in twins depends on the presentation of the:
opts: 1st twin – vertex allows vaginal delivery; breech/transverse lie needs C-section
questions.exp: Presentation of the 1st twin governs the route: vertex → vaginal, breech/transverse → C-section. (Book p471)

questions.q: Match delivery plans when the 1st twin is vertex: 2nd vertex, 2nd breech, 2nd transverse.
opts: Both vaginal; assisted breech delivery for 2nd; shift to OT with internal podalic version + breech extraction for 2nd
questions.exp: Vertex-vertex both vaginal; vertex-breech assisted breech; vertex-transverse internal podalic version and breech extraction in OT. (Book p471)

questions.q: After delivery of the 1st twin, which drug is contraindicated and why?
opts: Methylergometrine – it causes uterine contractions trapping the 2nd twin
questions.exp: Methylergometrine is c/i after the 1st twin as it contracts the uterus. (Book p471)

questions.q: The maximum acceptable time gap between delivery of the twins is ______; beyond it the action is ______.
opts: 30 minutes; immediate C-section of the 2nd twin
questions.exp: A gap >30 minutes mandates immediate C-section of the second twin. (Book p471)

questions.q: Internal podalic version has a single indication and one contraindication:
opts: 2nd twin in transverse lie; previous h/o C-section
questions.exp: IPV is indicated only for a transverse 2nd twin and c/i after previous C-section. (Book p471)

questions.q: Technique of internal podalic version:
opts: Under general anaesthesia a hand is inserted into the uterus, the baby's feet are held and rotated to convert to breech
Under spinal, forceps rotation of the head
questions.exp: Under GA the hand enters the uterus, grasps the feet and rotates the fetus to breech. (Book p471)

questions.q: The note adds that EXTERNAL cephalic version is attempted only if:
opts: The fetus is breech at 30 weeks
questions.exp: ECV requires intact membranes per the note. (Book p471)

units.title: Dizygotic vs monozygotic twins → Superfecundation, superfetation & risk factors
units.guide: Contrast dizygotic and monozygotic twins from formation to fingerprints, apply Hellin's rule and separate superfecundation from superfetation with their risk factors. Focus for this checkpoint: Dizygotic vs monozygotic twins, Superfecundation, superfetation & risk factors.

units.title: Chorionicity & amnionicity
units.guide: Time the zygote's division against membrane formation to predict DCDA, MCDA, MCMA or conjoined twins, and know why chorionicity drives prognosis and scan timing. Focus for this checkpoint: Chorionicity & amnionicity.

units.title: DCDA vs MCDA vs MCMA → USG in twin pregnancy & conjoined twins
units.sec: DCDA vs MCDA vs MCMA & twin USG · p463-464
units.guide: Read the membrane-layer, thickness, vascular-connection and lambda/T-sign table, then use twin ultrasound markers and conjoined-twin management. Focus for this checkpoint: DCDA vs MCDA vs MCMA, USG in twin pregnancy & conjoined twins.

units.title: Maternal complications & PIH prophylaxis → Fetal complications & fetal reduction
units.guide: List the exaggerated maternal physiology of twins, aspirin prophylaxis for PIH and the rules of aneuploidy sampling and fetal reduction. Focus for this checkpoint: Maternal complications & PIH prophylaxis, Fetal complications & fetal reduction.

units.title: Complications common to all twins → Death of one twin
units.sec: Common complications & death of one twin · p466-467
units.guide: Remember the three universal twin complications, the vanishing twin and the haemodynamic fate of a surviving monochorionic co-twin. Focus for this checkpoint: Complications common to all twins, Death of one twin.

units.title: Monochorionic-specific complications → etiopathogenesis & donor-recipient
units.guide: Distinguish selective IUGR from general IUGR and build the TTTS donor-recipient picture from anastomosis depth to MCA-PSV. Focus for this checkpoint: Monochorionic-specific complications, TTTS: etiopathogenesis & donor-recipient.

units.title: diagnosis & staging → follow-up & treatment
units.guide: Apply the poly-oligo criteria, stuck-twin physiology and Quintero stages, then choose laser ablation versus serial amnioreduction by gestational age. Focus for this checkpoint: TTTS: diagnosis & staging, TTTS: follow-up & treatment.

units.title: TAPS & TRAP → Selective IUGR & monoamniotic complications
units.guide: Separate TAPS from TTTS by normal fluid volumes, trace the acardiac twin of TRAP and manage cord entanglement in monoamniotic pregnancies. Focus for this checkpoint: TAPS & TRAP, Selective IUGR & monoamniotic complications.

units.title: Delivery in twin pregnancy
units.guide: Let the first twin's presentation decide the route, handle the transverse second twin with internal podalic version and respect the 30-minute gap rule. Focus for this checkpoint: Delivery in twin pregnancy.
